title: Serde deserialisation accepts a vector longer than its declared maximum and encodes undecodable bytes
severity_basis: JSON input with 21 signatures is accepted into a DecoratedSignature<20> and encoded; the library's own decoder refuses the bytes. Published advisory; fixed in 28.0.1.
caps_note: No CAP applies: a rule of SEP-51 XDR-JSON and the XDR definitions (a vector's declared maximum), not a protocol change (the corpus's xdr-json group).

entries.expected: refuse JSON whose vector exceeds the declared maximum
entries.observed: Executed on 28.0.0: serde deserialisation of the JSON accepts 21 signatures into a DecoratedSignature<20> and the encoder writes bytes the library's own decoder refuses; 28.0.1 refuses the JSON ('xdr value max length exceeded').

evidence.pre_fix: Conformance runner (xcc conform run --set all), L4, on rust@28.0.0 (both profiles).
evidence.post_fix: rust@28.0.1 and 30.0.0 refuse with "xdr value max length exceeded".
evidence.expected_basis: Transaction signatures are DecoratedSignature<20> in the XDR definitions (stellar-xdr v30.0).

reproduction.method: Independent reviewer reproduction from the record alone on 2026-11-12: 2 of 2 listed report rows failed again as recorded, all offline. Review: findings/review/F-0030.json.

evidence_added.reason: Fixed upstream; the upstream item already carries the reproduction and the fix, so no new evidence is added.

history.note: Created from the known divergences that reference https://github.com/stellar/rs-stellar-xdr/security/advisories/GHSA-3xhm-p452-9wjh and their failure rows.
The upstream item already records this defect.
